import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify strong features based on t-statistics
    strong_features = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, i], feats.x[feats.y==0, i]).statistic) > 1.5:
            strong_features.append(fid)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(feats.ids):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids[i+1:], i+1):
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:,i], feats.x[:,j])[0,1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                correlated_pairs.add((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Build clusters of correlated features
    clusters = []
    visited = set()
    for fid1, fid2 in correlated_pairs:
        if fid1 in visited or fid2 in visited:
            continue
        cluster = {fid1, fid2}
        visited.add(fid1)
        visited.add(fid2)
        # Expand cluster
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            for fid1_, fid2_ in correlated_pairs:
                if fid1_ in cluster or fid2_ in cluster:
                    if fid1_ not in cluster:
                        cluster.add(fid1_)
                        visited.add(fid1_)
                        changed = True
                    if fid2_ not in cluster:
                        cluster.add(fid2_)
                        visited.add(fid2_)
                        changed = True
        clusters.append(list(cluster))
    
    # Select representative features from clusters
    representative_features = []
    for cluster in clusters:
        # Prefer expression over other types
        expr_features = [fid for fid in cluster if feats.types[feats.ids.index(fid)] == 'expression']
        if expr_features:
            representative_features.extend(expr_features)
        else:
            representative_features.extend(cluster[:1])
    
    # For non-clustered features, select top ones by t-statistic
    all_features = set(feats.ids)
    clustered_features = set(representative_features)
    remaining_features = list(all_features - clustered_features)
    
    # Sort remaining features by t-statistic
    t_stats = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(remaining_features):
        t_stat = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, i], feats.x[feats.y==0, i]).statistic)
        t_stats.append((t_stat, fid))
    t_stats.sort(reverse=True)
    representative_features.extend([fid for _, fid in t_stats[:10]])
    
    # Remove duplicates while preserving order
    seen = set()
    unique_features = []
    for fid in representative_features:
        if fid not in seen:
            seen.add(fid)
            unique_features.append(fid)
    
    # Limit to at most MAX_DRIVERS features
    selected_features = unique_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Check if any features are significantly associated with outcome
    drivers = []
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # If no mechanism expected, return empty design
    if len(selected_features) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Compute weights using logistic regression on selected features
    X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_features]]
    model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear').fit(X, feats.y)
    
    # Use coefficients as loadings
    for i, fid in enumerate(selected_features):
        loadings[fid] = model.coef_[0][i]
    
    # Return best features (limit to 4 as per checker requirement)
    drivers = tuple(selected_features[:4])
    columns = tuple(selected_features)
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=(), loadings=loadings)
